name: Aqara Temperature and Humidity Sensor T1 (EU)

matter.note: No CSA listing found. Aqara says Matter-capable hubs such as the M3 can bridge Aqara Zigbee sensors, but no Aqara page seen confirms this for the T1.

apple_home.note: Aqara's HomeKit-via-hub wording seen is on the older Temperature and Humidity Sensor (WSDCGQ11LM) pages, not the T1's. Retailers list HomeKit for the T1, which isn't enough on its own.

google_home.note: Only retailer listings say Google Home works.

alexa.note: Only retailer listings say Alexa works.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant docs seen name no Aqara T1 support. A generic Zigbee coordinator is not documented for it.

hubRequired.note: Aqara's T1 FAQ says the sensor can't connect to a phone directly: add an Aqara hub first, then pair the sensor to the hub.

localControl.note: No page seen describes hub-local operation.

senses.note: It also measures air pressure (30–110 kPa), which the site does not list as a sensing type.

power.note: Aqara's T1 specs page says CR2032. Some Aqara pages for other temperature sensors say CR2450.

summary: The Temperature and Humidity Sensor T1 (TH-S02D) is Aqara's Zigbee 3.0 climate sensor. It reads temperature (±0.3 °C), humidity (±3%) and air pressure, and reports hourly unless values change sharply. It is for indoor use, runs on a CR2032 cell and pairs only through an Aqara hub.
caveats: Needs an Aqara hub; Aqara's T1 pages seen don't confirm Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa or SmartThings support.
